title: NPCs near V and picks
summary: npc.list reads the people near V and who may be directed (protected and busy ones named); npc.pick adopts an ordinary passer-by for look, face and speech; npc.status lists the session's actors, picks, lines, hub and casts.

demand.note: The people around V up to 40 m with crowd, protected and busy flags.

rows.note: A released pick stood about 20 s at a crossing before walking on; 0.8.9 sends it on at its normal pace.

limits: npc.pick needs the writer seat, because it reserves shared pick slots.

title: XF actors
summary: npc.spawn brings in XF actors: TweakXL clones of base-game civilians, never saved, friendly and immortal unless asked, at a point or relative to V with a sight line from her head.

demand.note: Spawn and despawn people with any record and appearance, friendly or hostile, at a chosen place, with an identity that survives streaming, at crowd scale.

rows.note: Spawned 8.25 m ahead facing V.
A spawn at a vending machine was visible (in session 16 it stood unseen; 0.8.10 needs a sight line).

limits: At most five XF actors (three before 0.8.19), within 30 m.
The npc write class and the XF actor records ship in the -writes package only.

known_issues.summary: The sight-line check rays against the Static collision group only; a device may not be in it, so an actor can still stand inside one unseen.

improvements.summary: Any record and appearance at crowd scale (V1): today ten cloned casts and five actors.

title: Directing movement
summary: npc.move, npc.follow, npc.turn, npc.place and npc.stop walk, follow, turn and place actors and picks through the game's own AI commands; a walk more than 80 degrees off the actor's facing begins with a turn on the spot.

demand.note: Direct people: walk or drive, use a workspot, follow or flee; set their attitude; fight in a group or surrender. Move, follow, turn and place are proven; no workspots, fleeing or fighting.

rows.note: Walked to V and arrived 2.13 m away.
Backwards after a walk to V: the facing target the move handler never clears. Fixed in 0.8.11, unverified.
The dissolve walked away forwards.

known_issues.summary: The turn-first walk rests on a hypothesis; close when N1 and N2 pass or the cause is named.
The facing-target argument's name is the behaviour tree's own; 0.8.11 clears FacingTarget by analogy, which does nothing if the name is wrong.

title: NPC lines
summary: npc.say gives an actor or pick a subtitle, an overhead line, a caller's subtitle (call_subtitle), a vanilla voice line in its own voice, or a voice with no body.

demand.note: Overhead text, subtitles and holocalls; the game's own lines by voice and by line. No chosen lines.

rows.note: The subtitle showed; the voiced greeting was the voice's own curt line.
call_subtitle shows as 'Caller: …'.

limits: A line given near_m is refused unless the NPC stands that close.

known_issues.summary: A voiceset's greeting is the voice's own line and can't be chosen (warm in one call, curt in the next); scenes speak subtitles, and a spoken chosen line has no route.

title: Dialogue choices with V
summary: npc.choices offers V two to four lines in the game's own dialogue widget, attached to an actor or pick; the pick comes back as npc.choice, and the hub is withdrawn when V leaves or a device screen takes over.

demand.note: Dialogue choices with V (2-4 choices in the game's widget, the pick returned: proven).

rows.note: Bridge-hub pick through the game's action handler without the player: highlight gave none, commit exactly one (20/20).

title: Face and gaze
summary: npc.look and npc.face set where an actor or pick looks and its expression; while the bridge directs it, the game's own look-at reaction (the angry face, the curt bark, the chest twist) is held back.

rows.note: The actor's own reactions won over the smile; 0.8.9 wraps the reaction system.
The reaction wraps held: a smile stayed 20 s face to face.
The scene's smile did not show; cause unresolved.

known_issues.summary: A held face is sent again (0.8 s, 2.5 s, then every 5 s) because session 17's smile didn't show and nothing says what took it; the resend may blip.

unknowns.question: What took session 17's smile: early delivery before the graph was ready, a later write, or downstream blending?
unknowns.settle_by: R3's discriminating probe (NPC face state §6) and RT5

title: Gestures
summary: npc.act plays a gesture (talk, wave, shrug, nod, arms crossed, facepalm, check phone) on an actor through an XF animation carrier.

known_issues.summary: The XF gesture carrier isn't built, so in the game every gesture answers carrier_missing.

title: Mortal and hostile stand-ins
summary: npc.spawn with attitude, immortal and reactions makes a stand-in that can be shot and turn hostile; a fight hands it back to its own AI instead of removing it, and a body stays until released.

demand.note: Mortal and hostile stand-ins that can be hurt and killed, turn hostile or hand back to AI, and keep the game's reaction presets.

rows.note: Handed back in the fight, died and kept its body; the police answered the shooting.

quirks: A civilian stand-in's death counts as a civilian's (the police respond); its death record says civilian true.

title: Combat stand-ins
summary: Two casts cloned from tier-1 gang grunts (fighter_melee with bare fists, fighter_pistol with a handgun) fight V with their own AI; engage:true puts V in the actor's threat list through the game's own route; they sit in an isolated attitude group.

demand.note: Hostile stand-ins that actually start a fight (civilian casts never did).

rows.note: Optional.

limits: Immortal by default; never saved; -writes package only.

unknowns.question: Can the aggressive reaction preset turn a fighter hostile to whoever fires near it, despite the isolated group?

title: Out-of-sight staging
summary: npc.spawn with out_of_sight picks a walkable spot V can't see; npc.release with dissolve removes an actor only once it is out of her sight.

demand.note: Spawn outside V's view and hearing; dissolve by walking away and despawning out of sight; join a scene mid-phase, posed, with no visible fast-forward (not built).

rows.note: Landed 12 m behind V unseen.
The dissolve waited until V looked away.

improvements.summary: Join a scene mid-phase, posed, with no visible fast-forward (V16's last part).

title: Crowd substitution
summary: npc.substitute replaces a plain passer-by of the street crowd with an XF actor of the same look, unseen: it holds the original still, spawns the actor at its spot once V can't see it, and hides the original only when the actor stands there; every failed swap gives the original back.

demand.note: Adopt crowd people into the simulation (route a: substitution with the same look), keep identity across reloads through the resident key and respawn parameters, release cleanly.

rows.note: Borg 4's swap fell back on the look (asked creole_11, got a king_of_the_stoop appearance).
Swapped 19 m away out of V's view within 0.8 s; the maintainer saw nothing odd.
Released with restore as a despawn (not a dissolve); a fresh crowd person came 2.9 s later rather than the original.
Borg 4 saw the npc_busy, npc_protected and too_far refusals right, not the community refusal.

limits: Lane-crowd walkers only: community NPCs are refused (community_npc), because a quest reservation can't be detected and the removal can't be undone.
quirks: restore leaves a fresh crowd person, not the original; acceptable for crowds.
resident.key is ours (a hash of record, appearance and spawn spot), not the game's.

unknowns.question: Which of HideIrreversibly's effects remain until recycling; does AIJoinCrowdCommand return a spawned crowd person to the lanes; does the clone flee gunfire?

improvements.summary: Count look fall-backs and widen the candidate appearance search (Borg 4).

title: Adopting the game's own crowd people
summary: Take over a person the crowd system spawned (hold or replace their AI), run them on the engine's routine and release them back to the lanes, keeping a stable identity for community people.

demand.note: Route (b): adopt, direct, release the game's crowd body; key stability across a reload (CA1 to CA7).

unknowns.question: Does a move command work on a live lane walker, does release return it to the lane, and is the community key stable across a reload?

title: Directing protected people
summary: Direct people the game protects (vendors, police, quest-adjacent people) for a staged moment, or stand them in with a clone in their look and place while the original is hidden.

demand.note: Not built; plan around stand-ins. Hiding and restoring someone else's NPC and holding a crowd NPC's AI are unproven, and quest reservation can't be detected safely.

title: Scenes written as data
summary: npc.scenario runs a scene written as data (the first is 'a stranger with a question'), releasing every actor it brought in however it ends.

rows.note: Walked backwards and spoke before arriving.
The bark was its own greeting step; still a backwards walk away.
The smile didn't show; the walk away went backwards.

notes: The plan module (supervisor.plan-module) is the general successor for scenes; npc.scenario stays the tools-side scene runner until then.
